markdown_report:
At 10% progress, select a small, controlled extension: **specificity-gated repeated-support lexical fusion**. Its benefit remains untested.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Repeated support offers an identifiable historical connection. Distinct item IDs reduce self-reinforcement, although product variants can still inflate evidence. (2) Recency can attenuate stale interests. It cannot establish whether a purchase satisfied a need. (3) Fixed lexical features make support inspectable. Adding a learned encoder and auxiliary loss simultaneously would obscure attribution; the supplied fixed-residual result, 0.5587, motivates retaining a simple comparator.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) and [Dross Into Gold](https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23) motivate objective controls. Their results do not establish which loss wins here. (2) [LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) separates persistent and recent interests. This motivates conditioning historical evidence on current context. (3) [DTR4Rec](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10489-024-05875-3) motivates directional associations. Such associations do not establish compatibility or complementarity.

The framework separates three directions: discrimination through the objective, evidence selection through lexical specificity and recency, and directional prediction through transitions. These address different uncertainties and should initially be tested separately.

| Idea | O/P/U/M/D scores | Assessment: positive; negative |
|---|---|---|
| Matched multi-negative objective comparison | 2/7/3/8/3 | O: controlled application; established. P: reusable; gains unknown. U: better ranking; no explicit intent mechanism. M: targets pair errors; calibration unproven. D: localized changes; matching exposure requires care. |
| Specificity-gated lexical residual | 4/7/8/6/5 | O: explicit candidate evidence gate; incremental. P: inspectable; vocabulary brittle. U: targets broad and stale matches; misses complements. M: combined-score supervision; generalization unknown. D: fixed features; causal sparse scoring needs care. |
| Recent-source directed-transition residual | 4/7/6/6/6 | O: combines established components; substantial prior art. P: captures follow-ons; sparse edges. U: recent identifiable links; usefulness unverified. M: extra ranking signal; popularity confounding. D: sparse counts; leakage-safe construction required. |

Scores denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

**Chosen algorithm.** Keep the incumbent recency-weighted, distinct-item TF–IDF pool. Admit candidate residual evidence only through sufficiently uncommon tokens occurring in at least two distinct recent historical items and in the candidate. Freeze token eligibility from training-document frequencies before validation; test a declared threshold rather than selecting words from feedback. Confidence remains outside normalization, and the residual amplitude starts at zero.

This explicitly targets broad associations and stale or isolated historical demand. Combined-score multi-negative training targets weak sampled-pair separation, especially Electronics’ supplied 16.98% error rate; that statistic does not establish validation improvement.

Compare objective-only, unchanged lexical residual, and gated residual with matched settings. Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, retaining the incumbent on ties. Preserve routing, seeds, predictor parity, diagnostic contracts, and the remaining shared budget. No compatibility, ownership, simulator-trait, or test-performance claims follow from lexical overlap.

idea.description: Add a candidate-specific uncommon-token gate to the fixed repeated-support lexical residual, retaining per-dataset SASRec and matched multi-negative training. A candidate receives lexical evidence only from tokens shared with at least two distinct recent historical item IDs. This is an incremental, untested extension intended to distinguish specific recurring interests from broad textual associations.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations, stale historical demand, and recommendations lacking an identifiable connection. Repeated uncommon-token evidence supplies an inspectable connection, while recent-window recency weights attenuate old and isolated evidence. Combined-score training targets the model diagnosis of weak sampled training-pair separation, particularly Electronics. Neither lexical overlap nor training margins establishes current need, compatibility, or validation gains.
idea.implementation_notes:
Return this as an implementation specification; no execution or new result is claimed. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged splits and dataset routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS with effective default 200. Use only histories, titles, descriptions, and observed timestamps; the generic metadata examples do not authorize unavailable fields.

Retain the incumbent TF–IDF preprocessing, vocabulary scope, support rule, optimizer, and checkpoint schedule where compatible artifacts exist. A scalar historical result alone does not establish compatibility. If reimplementing, declare the complete configuration and rerun the matched comparator. Fit vocabulary and document frequencies only on items appearing in training histories, then transform permitted catalog text with the frozen vocabulary. Missing or out-of-vocabulary text gives a zero row.

For a declared initial configuration, use a 20-event window, latest-occurrence deduplication by item ID, and event half-life 5. For each causal prefix, compute the incumbent fixed TF–IDF agreement weights and confidence c. Select eligible tokens with training-item document frequency at least 2 and at most 5% of training-observed items; freeze this threshold before validation. This threshold is a hypothesis rather than an optimized setting. Let b_t indicate that eligible token t occurs in at least two distinct window items. Form z = p elementwise-multiplied by b, where p is the incumbent normalized pool. Do not renormalize z: removing unsupported dimensions should attenuate evidence rather than amplify the remainder. Score candidate i as h dot e_i + alpha*c*(z dot x_i). Because z is a masked unit-norm vector and x_i is normalized, the nonnegative lexical similarity is bounded by 1. Initialize alpha directly at zero, exclude it from weight decay, and project it into [0,1] after each update. The cap is scale-sensitive and must be reported alongside collaborative and residual logit scales. Compare with the unchanged residual to isolate the gate.

Use positive-plus-32-negative sampled cross-entropy for every primary condition. Draw uniform negatives with a dedicated seed-42 generator, excluding padding, the target, and causal-prefix items. Mask unused slots when eligible items are insufficient; skip positions without eligible negatives. This is a sampled ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Match initialization, candidate streams, backbone, optimizer, and training exposure across objective-only, unchanged-residual, and gated-residual conditions. A separate BCE/gBCE comparison is a follow-up, not evidence supplied by this experiment.

Compute support from prefix inputs only, never from the target or future events. Use sparse CSR text rows and bounded window operations, avoiding catalog-wide pairwise similarities. Full-catalog simulator scoring must use blocks and historical-item exclusion for twenty real training users, five per category. Pinned candidate scoring must preserve the evaluator's supplied candidate order and masking behavior.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model remains the trained nn.Module. Retain item_emb, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility. Adapt log2feats and predict_score through a documented feature representation carrying collaborative features plus causal context information, so positive/negative probes use the deployed combined scorer. Restore model mode after eval/no_grad probes. Add defined gate activation, removed lexical mass, distinct supporting IDs, residual scale, and candidate rank-change diagnostics. Keep embedding cosine descriptive and unavailable category breakdowns explicitly unavailable.

Update the predictor writer to serialize and load model weights, routing, vocabulary, IDF, sparse item rows, token eligibility, pooling settings, amplitude, and architecture configuration. Verify training/predictor score parity on training-visible fixtures including empty histories, missing text, repeated IDs, two-item support, ubiquitous words, and mixed routes. Verify that future events cannot alter earlier scores.

Subtract prior charged work from 43,200 GPU-seconds before admitting trials. Training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures share the remainder; reserve capacity for export and parity checks. Compare only complete four-category runs under the pinned validation protocol, retain the incumbent on exact ties, record all validation queries and costs, and freeze selection before held-out inference. The supplied 0.5587 and 0.5538 results are historical observations, not new measurements or proof of a general mechanism. Track simulator broad-match, stale-interest, uncertain-content, and useful-complement judgments only when actually supplied. The gate can suppress synonyms, sparse interests, and useful complements, and can still reward near-duplicate products.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG: retain four baseline routes; preprocessing_seed=0; training_seed=42
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']

for category in baseline_categories:
    X, vocabulary, df = fit_training_only_tfidf_or_load_compatible_artifacts()
    eligible_token = (df >= 2) & (df <= 0.05 * training_item_count)
    initialize_matched_SASRec(seed=42)
    alpha = trainable_scalar(0.0)

    for batch in unchanged_training_loader:
        h = model.log2feats(batch.sequence)
        for each valid position t:
            prefix = batch.sequence through t
            ids, ages = latest_distinct_ids(prefix.last_20_events)
            p, c = incumbent_fixed_support_pool(X[ids], ages)
            occurrence_count = count_distinct_item_rows_containing_each_token(X[ids])
            supported = eligible_token & (occurrence_count >= 2)
            z = p * supported  # deliberately do not renormalize
            candidates, mask = positive_plus_uniform_negatives(
                positive=batch.positive[t], count=32,
                exclude=padding_and_target_and_prefix_ids,
                rng=dedicated_seed_42_generator)
            logits = dot(h[t], item_emb(candidates))
            logits += alpha * c * sparse_dot(z, X[candidates])
        optimize(masked_sampled_cross_entropy(logits, positive_index=0))
        project_alpha_to_interval(0, 1)
        honor_existing_checkpoint_schedule_and_remaining_budget()

    export_trial_local_artifacts_and_matching_predictor_writer()
    verify_training_visible_causal_and_score_parity_fixtures()
    run_adapted_DiagnosisProbe_on_actual_model()

# Controlled conditions: objective-only, incumbent residual, gated residual.
# Select complete four-category configurations using pinned macro validation HR@10.
# Retain incumbent on ties. Never consult hidden test labels.

originality.positive: Candidate-specific uncommon-token recurrence makes the evidence gate explicit and independently ablatable.
originality.negative: TF–IDF profiles, recency weighting, support filtering, and additive scoring are established; novelty is incremental and not established by an exhaustive literature review.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inspectable baseline for studying whether specific repeated evidence improves current-interest ranking before adding learned semantic capacity.
future_potential.negative: Exact-token support misses paraphrases and sparse emerging interests, and cannot establish compatibility, unmet demand, or complementarity.

code_difficulty.positive: Fixed text features and one scalar preserve the SASRec backbone and avoid training another encoder.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal sparse masking, matched controls, diagnostic feature transport, full-catalog scoring, and predictor serialization require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequence encoder and item-scoring baseline.
limitations: Does not supply the proposed explicit lexical evidence gate or establish current unmet needs.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates examining generalized BCE and negative-sampling effects before adding model capacity.
limitations: Reported gains do not establish improvement under this Amazon protocol; changes in calibration and negative count require matched controls.

related_work.title: Turning Dross Into Gold Loss
contributions: Supplies a practical multi-negative cross-entropy direction for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Objective changes alone do not explicitly distinguish specific current interests from broad or stale associations.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Motivates separating persistent interests from recent behavior.
limitations: Does not establish identifiable intent or validate the proposed lexical gate on these four datasets.

related_work.title: DTR4Rec
contributions: Motivates directed transition and short-window association signals as an alternative research direction.
limitations: Predictive transitions do not establish compatibility, complementarity, or unmet demand.
